Compare three drift detection methods on a synthetic dataset with
engineered distribution shift:

- **KS / Chi-squared** — univariate per-column tests
- **PSI** — Population Stability Index with severity classification
- **Domain Classifier** — multivariate drift via AUC of a classifier

## 1. Create Reference & Shifted Datasets

```{python}
#| label: create-datasets
#| cache: true
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification

np.random.seed(42)
X_ref, y_ref = make_classification(
    n_samples=2000, n_features=10, n_informative=6, random_state=42
)
df_ref = pl.DataFrame({f"feat_{i}": X_ref[:, i] for i in range(X_ref.shape[1])})
df_ref = df_ref.with_columns(target=pl.Series(y_ref))

X_live = X_ref[:800].copy()
X_live[:, 0] += 1.5
X_live[:, 3] *= 1.8
X_live[:, 7] += np.random.normal(0, 3, size=800)
df_live = pl.DataFrame({f"feat_{i}": X_live[:, i] for i in range(X_live.shape[1])})
df_live = df_live.with_columns(target=pl.Series(y_ref[:800]))
print(f"Reference: {df_ref.shape}  |  Live: {df_live.shape}  |  Shifted columns: feat_0, feat_3, feat_7")
```

```{python}
#| label: distribution-overlay
#| fig-cap: "Reference (blue) vs Live (orange) distributions for drifted and stable features"
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.5
shifted_cols = [0, 3, 7]
stable_cols = [1, 2]
cols_to_plot = shifted_cols + stable_cols

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(cols_to_plot), figsize=(12, 3.5))
for ax, col_idx in zip(axes, cols_to_plot):
    ax.hist(X_ref[:, col_idx], bins=40, alpha=0.5, density=True, label="Reference", color="#4C72B0")
    ax.hist(X_live[:, col_idx], bins=40, alpha=0.5, density=True, label="Live", color="#DD8452")
    label = "DRIFTED" if col_idx in shifted_cols else "stable"
    ax.set_title(f"feat_{col_idx} ({label})", fontsize=10,
                 color="#C44E52" if col_idx in shifted_cols else "#55A868")
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)

plt.suptitle("Distribution Comparison: Reference vs Live", fontsize=12, y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 2. KS / Chi-squared Drift Detection

```{python}
#| label: ks-drift
#| cache: true
from iter8ml.monitoring.drift import DriftDetector

ks_detector = DriftDetector(df_ref, alpha=0.05)
ks_report = ks_detector.detect(df_live)
print(f"Drift detected: {ks_report.drift_detected}  |  Columns drifted: {ks_report.n_drifted}/{ks_report.n_columns_tested}")
```

```{python}
#| label: ks-drift-chart
#| fig-cap: "KS test p-values per feature — red dashed line is the significance threshold (alpha=0.05)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
features = [c.column for c in ks_report.column_results]
p_values = [c.p_value for c in ks_report.column_results]
drifted = [c.drift_detected for c in ks_report.column_results]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
colors = ["#C44E52" if d else "#55A868" for d in drifted]
bars = ax.barh(features, p_values, color=colors)
ax.axvline(0.05, color="#C44E52", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label="alpha = 0.05")
ax.set_xlabel("p-value")
ax.set_title("KS/Chi-squared Drift Detection per Feature")
ax.legend()
ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 3. PSI (Population Stability Index)

```{python}
#| label: psi-drift
#| cache: true
from iter8ml.monitoring.psi_drift import PSIDriftDetector

psi_detector = PSIDriftDetector(df_ref, n_bins=10)
psi_report = psi_detector.detect(df_live)
print(f"PSI drift detected: {psi_report.drift_detected}  |  Moderate: {psi_report.n_moderate}  |  Severe: {psi_report.n_severe}")
```

```{python}
#| label: psi-chart
#| fig-cap: "PSI values per feature with severity thresholds (green < 0.1, orange 0.1-0.25, red > 0.25)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
psi_features = [f.feature for f in psi_report.feature_psi]
psi_values = [f.psi_value for f in psi_report.feature_psi]
psi_levels = [f.drift_level for f in psi_report.feature_psi]

level_colors = {"none": "#55A868", "moderate": "#DD8452", "severe": "#C44E52"}
bar_colors = [level_colors.get(l, "#888888") for l in psi_levels]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
bars = ax.barh(psi_features, psi_values, color=bar_colors)
ax.axvline(0.1, color="#DD8452", linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label="Moderate (0.1)")
ax.axvline(0.25, color="#C44E52", linestyle="--", linewidth=1, label="Severe (0.25)")
ax.set_xlabel("PSI Value")
ax.set_title("Population Stability Index per Feature")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 4. Domain Classifier (Multivariate Drift)

```{python}
#| label: domain-classifier
#| cache: true
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import RocCurveDisplay
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_predict
from iter8ml.monitoring.domain_classifier import DomainClassifierDriftDetector

dc_detector = DomainClassifierDriftDetector(df_ref, threshold=0.7, random_seed=42)
dc_report = dc_detector.detect(df_live)
print(f"AUC: {dc_report.auc_score:.4f}  |  Threshold: {dc_report.threshold}  |  Drift: {dc_report.drift_detected}")
```

```{python}
#| label: domain-classifier-roc
#| fig-cap: "Domain classifier ROC curve — AUC > 0.7 indicates the classifier can distinguish reference from live data (drift detected)"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5
ref_np = df_ref.drop("target").to_numpy()
live_np = df_live.drop("target").to_numpy()
X_combined = np.vstack([ref_np, live_np])
y_combined = np.concatenate([np.zeros(len(ref_np)), np.ones(len(live_np))])

clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
y_score = cross_val_predict(clf, X_combined, y_combined, cv=3, method="predict_proba")[:, 1]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
RocCurveDisplay.from_predictions(y_combined, y_score, ax=ax, color="#4C72B0")
ax.axvline(1 - dc_report.threshold, color="#C44E52", linestyle="--", alpha=0.7,
           label=f"Drift threshold (TPR @ {dc_report.threshold})")
ax.set_title(f"Domain Classifier ROC (AUC = {dc_report.auc_score:.3f})")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 5. Methods Comparison Summary

```{python}
#| label: methods-summary
#| fig-cap: "Side-by-side comparison of all three drift detection methods"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 4))

ks_status = ["DRIFT" if c.drift_detected else "OK" for c in ks_report.column_results]
ks_colors = ["#C44E52" if c.drift_detected else "#55A868" for c in ks_report.column_results]
axes[0].barh([c.column for c in ks_report.column_results],
             [-np.log10(c.p_value + 1e-300) for c in ks_report.column_results],
             color=ks_colors)
axes[0].axvline(-np.log10(0.05), color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
axes[0].set_xlabel("-log10(p-value)")
axes[0].set_title("KS/Chi-squared")
axes[0].invert_yaxis()

psi_colors = [level_colors.get(l, "#888") for l in psi_levels]
axes[1].barh(psi_features, psi_values, color=psi_colors)
axes[1].axvline(0.1, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
axes[1].axvline(0.25, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
axes[1].set_xlabel("PSI")
axes[1].set_title("PSI")
axes[1].invert_yaxis()

methods = ["KS/Chi-squared", "PSI", "Domain Classifier"]
detected = [ks_report.drift_detected, psi_report.drift_detected, dc_report.drift_detected]
mcolors = ["#C44E52" if d else "#55A868" for d in detected]
axes[2].barh(methods, [1 if d else 0 for d in detected], color=mcolors)
axes[2].set_xlim(0, 1.3)
axes[2].set_xticks([0, 1])
axes[2].set_xticklabels(["No Drift", "Drift"])
axes[2].set_title("Drift Detected?")
axes[2].invert_yaxis()
for i, (m, d) in enumerate(zip(methods, detected)):
    axes[2].text(0.5 if d else 0.5, i, "YES" if d else "NO",
                 ha="center", va="center", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color="white")

plt.suptitle("Drift Detection Methods Comparison", fontsize=13, y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
